4 انشزهُ He raised it, (A, Msb, K,) namely, a place, (Msb,) or a thing, (K,) from its place. (A, K.) ―
-b2- [Hence,] انشز عِظَامَ المَيِّتِ He [God] raised the bones of the dead to their places, and set them, or put them together, one upon another. (S, K.) So in the Kur, [ii. 261,] وَٱنْظُرْ إِلَى ٱلْعِظَامِ كَيْفَ نُنْشِزُهَا ثُمَّ نَكْسُوهَا لَحْمًا [And look thou at the bones (of thine ass), how we raise them to their places, &c., then we clothe them with flesh], accord. to the reading of Zeyd Ibn-Thábit; (Fr, S, * TA;) but the Koofees read [نُنْشِرُهَا] with rá: the former reading, however, accord. to Th, is preferred. (TA.) [See art. نشر.] ―
-b3- Hence also, انشر الرَّضَاعُ العَظْمَ (tropical:) The sucking of the breast increased, or augmented, the bone: as also انشرهُ, with rá. (Msb.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
